It is one thing to ask what you should do in these situations. It's another to find out what you will actually do. And you cannot know until it happens. Everyone as a "fight-or-flight response", and everyone's is different. You may want to be a hero, you may want to run, you may want to hide. In the first instant your subconscious will decide your first move. Usually, that move is to duck or dive. Some people lock up like those fainting goats, others immediately address the threat. So your may not calculate your first plan until 15-40 seconds after the event begins, maybe longer. By this point, your plan has to be adjusted to meet your mental and physical situation. You may have no choice but to fight, hide, continue running.

Have you ever been in a bar fight? How did it go? We're you able to slow down your emotions and react to the situation. Or did you walk away afterwards with no idea what really happened. I've seen some badass athletic types get their ass kicked by fat dumpy guys. The sports guys only real life experience was in sports with a tacit understanding that we are playing a game and we will stop short of injuring each other, or a referee will keep you from injuring me. But the fat ass grew up with an abusive dad or older brother and getting punched in the face wasn't an unfamiliar situation. Athlete gets punched, pushed threatened and freezes, fat ass gets punched pushed or threatened and his fight response kicks in.

My point is that the idea of having a plan in that situation might be dangerous, because you may convince yourself to do something that your physical or mental situation isn't capable of following through with. So the only way to really prepare for that situation is to train. And I don't mean just do some target practice, or take some karate classes. You have to train your mind by scaring it. Go to a boxing gym and spar, so you can train your brain to react while dealing with an attack. Better yet get some boxing gloves and backyard brawl with friends. People always get pissed and carried away, this is a better simulation then actual fighting. Learn to relax and slow down your thinking. Things like this are about the best training, because obviously, you can't practice attacking someone while they are shooting at you. And paintball or pretend shooting won't fool your brain into that fear state so it is only minimally helpful.

So here's your plan. Subject enters crowd and starts shooting. Breathe. Slow down your thinking. Try to calm your emotions. Assess the situation you are in and what your body is willing to do .
